newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Forecast-FCL Paper loss seen deepening.
newsitem.headline: Forecast-FCL Paper loss seen deepening.

text.p: Fletcher Challenge Paper is expected to plunge deeper into loss when it reports its annual result next week, reflecting entirely its exposure to this stage of the pulp and paper cycle, analysts said on Friday.

Analysts expect FCL Paper's reported loss to come in at around NZ$60-70 million, after the inclusion of an extraordinary gain of about NZ$45 million -- the benefit from the sale of Canadian businesses.
In March, FCL Paper reported a first half loss of NZ$40 million and analysts expect the June year to represent the blackest part of the cycle.

Modest price improvements already in the pipeline meant FCL Paper was likely to return to profitability in the current year, but anything exceeding 1995/6's profit of NZ$177 million was seen as highly unlikely.

While pulp prices had started to show a belated improvement, conditions for most of FCL Paper's products throughout most of the fiscal year were "pretty awful," Doyle Paterson Brown analyst David Stanley said.
FCL Canada's result, reported on July 30, gave a taste of things to come.
Excluding restructuring expenses, FCL Canada's continuing operations incurred a net loss of C$16.1 million, down from the previous year's net earnings of C$154.8 million.
FCL Canada also faces the prospect of a strike at three British Columbia mills if agreements are not reached.
FCl Paper is one of the world's biggest newsprint producers and, while the outlook for some products was mixed, that for newsprint appeared favourable.
"In this industry, you go through periods where you lose money if you're highly sensitive to the cycle," Stanley said. "Other times you make pretty reasonable money.
"Being a cyclical business means that you do get these quite big swings," he said.
Looking ahead, analysts expect the key issues to be FCL's plans for U.K. Paper and its part in any rationalisation of the European fine paper industry.
Likewise, markets would be looking to how FCL Paper's overall business strategy was developing.
Guy Hallwright at First NZ Capital expects a reported loss of around NZ$60 million, based entirely on low prices, but he also sees return to modest profitability in the current year.
While the outlook had improved, there was a significant negative if the strike in British Columbia went ahead.
"Next year should be much better and we have the company going into profit in that year," he said.
FCL Paper last traded at NZ$3.52.
